_artifact: Meal_Plan_Store table definition — committed description, not applied infrastructure.
_comment: This file records the intended shape of the Meal_Plan_Store table so the definition is
reviewable in git. Nothing in this repository creates the table; provisioning is an
ordered human step documented in infra/README.md.
The 'createTable' object below is a valid dynamodb:CreateTable request body and can be
extracted verbatim; every other key is descriptive.
_regionRationale: Requirement 13.6 places the Meal_Plan_Store in the same region as the AI inference
and AWS_REGION defaults to us-east-1, so the table is pinned to us-east-1 and the Vercel
functions are pinned to iad1. MEAL_PLAN_AWS_REGION must equal AWS_REGION.
Changing this value alone is not a migration: the table, MEAL_PLAN_AWS_REGION, AWS_REGION,
the preferredRegion export on every route, and the IAM policy resource ARN move together.
_keySchemaRationale: Requirement 7.1: the owning User_Id is the partition key and the Meal_Plan_Id is the sort
key, so no record can be stored without an owner and no read can span owners. There is no
index that would allow a cross-owner read; see 'globalSecondaryIndexes' below.
_billingModeRationale: Requirement 13.3: PAY_PER_REQUEST has no minimum provisioned-capacity charge, so a month
with zero records and zero requests bills $0.00. Do not switch to PROVISIONED.
_sseRationale: Requirement 12.6: records are kept encrypted at rest. DynamoDB encrypts every table at
rest unconditionally; SSESpecification only selects which key does it.
SSESpecification.Enabled=false selects the AWS owned key, which is the default and costs
$0.00. Setting it to true switches to an AWS managed KMS key and starts billing KMS
requests, which the cost estimate in docs/hosting.md does not budget for.
So: 'Enabled: false' means 'encrypted at rest with the AWS owned key', not 'unencrypted'.
Consequence for verification: DescribeTable omits SSEDescription entirely for an AWS owned
key, so a smoke check must treat an absent SSEDescription as the expected state rather than
_deletionProtectionRationale: Not required by the spec. Enabled deliberately: this table holds health-related data and
the only supported way to remove a Patient's records is the Account_Deletion_Flow, which
deletes items and never the table. Deletion protection blocks dynamodb:DeleteTable only;
it does not affect DeleteItem, BatchWriteItem, or TransactWriteItems, so Requirement 11.3
_indexRationale: None. Every access pattern in the design is a GetItem or a Query pinned to one userId
partition; an index keyed on anything else would create the cross-owner read path that
Requirement 7.2 forbids, and would add write cost for no functional gain.
_ttlRationale: Off. Records are removed only on an explicit Patient action (Requirements 8.1, 11.3).
Silent expiry would delete a Patient's saved plans with no request behind it.
_pitrRationale: Off, per the design's table schema and the $0.00 backup line in the cost estimate. PITR is
off by default, so no post-create call is needed; the checklist step is to confirm it, not
to change it. PITR is also a continuous copy of health-related data, and the Account
deletion path in Requirement 11 has no story for purging a Patient from a backup window.

#meta: One item per Account holding planCount (Requirements 5.8, 5.9) and storageAckAt
(Requirements 12.3, 12.4). Not a Patient record. '#' (0x23) sorts strictly below every
Crockford base-32 ULID character, so the listing query excludes it with the key
condition mealPlanId > '#meta' rather than a post-filter, and Requirement 7.8's
letters-digits-hyphens charset rejects it before any store access.

PENDING#DELETION: Holds one item per User_Id whose purge did not complete (Requirement 11.7), keyed by
that User_Id in the sort key. Not an Account. Cannot collide with a Firebase uid,

_operatorNote: Both are internal bookkeeping. Do not create, edit, or delete them by hand in the
console: planCount and storageAckAt are maintained transactionally alongside the record
writes, and editing one out of band breaks the record cap or re-shows the storage notice.

recordAttributes.userId: S — partition key, the User_Id derived from the verified Auth_Token
recordAttributes.mealPlanId: S — sort key, 26-character Crockford base-32 ULID
recordAttributes.title: S — 1..100 as written by the API
recordAttributes.createdAt: S — ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 3 fractional digits
recordAttributes.updatedAt: S — ISO-8601 UTC, exactly 3 fractional digits
recordAttributes.content: M — { meals: L, summary: S, warnings: L (omitted when absent) }
_collectionNote: Every collection is an L list. No SS, NS, or BS attribute appears anywhere, because set
types are unordered and Requirements 6.4 and 9.3 depend on meal, item, and warning order

_operationsNote: This list mirrors infra/meal-plan-store-policy.json and must stay in step with it.
dynamodb:DeleteItem is required even though the adapter constructs no DeleteItemCommand:
removals are Delete entries inside TransactWriteItems and BatchWriteItem, and DynamoDB
dynamodb:Scan is absent by design (Requirements 7.2, 7.5): a Scan is the one DynamoDB
read that spans partitions, so withholding the permission means no future code path can
read across Accounts even by mistake. src/lib/server/dynamoMealPlanRepository.ts does not
import ScanCommand for the same reason.
